subject: Novacart renewal: benchmarking request and contingency / growth bridge
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@novacart.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal timeline + performance check before commit

Kim,

We’re starting the renewal conversation for Novacart (contract ends 2027-01-15) and I need two things from Redwood before we can move forward to procurement:

1) A short benchmark that reproduces our peak checkout flow (60–80 concurrent users, 1.2k tokens avg).
2) A firm offer for a 6–12 month bridge that includes a capacity uplift (we anticipate +2.5x token volume next quarter).

We’ve been approached by AtlasAI; they claim lower token latency and a lower sustained unit cost. Without performance numbers from Redwood we can’t justify the renewal to our CTO/procurement.

Can you propose a benchmark plan and a renewal bridge offer this week? Procurement (procurement@novacart.com) is cc’d here.

Thanks — Sophie
Sophie Turner
Head of Search & Personalization, Novacart

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask.

Short answer: we can run a focused benchmark + provide a short-term capacity/price bridge. Proposed next steps:

- Bench: 10 business day sandbox run using your anonymized checkout traces; we’ll validate latency and failure envelopes and produce a token-cost report. (Attachment: bench-plan.md)
- Bridge offer: 6-month term with a guaranteed burst pool to cover +2.5x peak. We’ll hold a price floor for the length of the bridge and include a performance credit (10% credit applied if benchmarks don’t meet agreed SLOs).
- Dedicated test: we can spin a dedicated pool for the bakeoff if you need tenant isolation.

Can you confirm: a) sample traces for the benchmark, b) your target P95 latency under load, c) procurement SLAs we should reference? I’ll pull in engineering and CS to scope the test.

Attaching a draft save plan and the capacity commitment sheet for procurement to review.

—Kimberly Park

Options I’m thinking for a save:
- Option A: 6-month renewal at current unit price + dedicated burst pool and 10% performance credit if bakeoff fails.
- Option B: 12-month commit with modest discount (12%) in exchange for capacity reservation and a short on-prem proxy for KV retention.
- Option C: Short-term discount + prioritize kernel optimizations during the trial to hit latency.

Need: benchmark plan, estimated engineering uplift/time, expected delta in cost for dedicated pool, and a suggested commercial term to present to procurement tomorrow.

Can Marcus and Rishi give a quick feasibility callout? Marissa / Neha — I’ll need your guidance on how aggressive we can be on discount and commit.

Quick technical readout:

- Bench approach: run two controlled experiments — (1) baseline with current production model and settings, (2) optimized run with continuous batching, KV-prefix caching enabled, and a quantized variant for cost comparison.
- Data needed: anonymized checkout traces (request/response sizes, token distributions). If they can provide traces within 48 hours we can stand up the runs in ~7 business days and deliver a report in 10.
- Dedicated pool: doable. Cost delta estimated at +18–22% for the dedicated burst pool to guarantee capacity and isolation during the test window.
- Latency: P95 target of 350ms is aggressive but achievable with the optimized run and dedicated pool; the quantized variant will save cost (~25%) but may increase P95 slightly — recommend a fallback policy: use full-precision model for tail latency-sensitive routes, quantized variant for background requests.

I’ll push a bench-plan.md to the thread (attached) with the exact script and sample metrics we’ll collect.

—Marcus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Sophie / Alan — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarity.

Summarizing the plan we’ll run if you agree:

1) Redwood will run a 10-business-day sandbox benchmark using your anonymized checkout traces. Marcus & team will run two experiments (baseline + optimized).
2) We’ll provision a dedicated burst pool for the 30-day isolation window (cost delta ~ +20% during the window).
3) Commercial bridge: 6 months at current unit price with a 10% performance credit if the P95 objective is not met; alternately we can do 12 months at a 12% discount if you commit to a capacity reservation.
4) If benchmarks pass, we’ll include a runway for a gradual capacity uplift (we can tier the +2.5x volume in two phases to keep tail latency stable).

Attachments: redwood_save_plan_v3.pdf, capacity_commitment_sheet.xlsx, bench-plan.md (technical script).
